data.body:
RP-01 residual usage-consumer audit complete. `.joe-janitor/rp01-usage-compat-probe.py` supplied `{requests: 1, candidate_requests: 3}` to the current compatibility paths and proved `candidate_requests` is dropped at 4/4 boundaries: Pass-1 `usage_record`, `aggregate_usage`, sanitized failure diagnostics, and the durable usage JSONL row. The research brief now records the full propagation obligation.

No production consumer requires `requests == 1` or means accepted-attempt-only. Consumers use it for Pydantic request-limit/headroom consumption, a `>0` verifier-ran proof, completion-recovery budget banking, and aggregate telemetry; pricing uses token fields, not requests. Returning whole-Agent-run requests/usage after a successful retry therefore makes those consumers more truthful and preserves one durable row per outer Rebar operation.

For the additive counter, the implementation must keep `requests` as Pydantic's request-budget count and carry `candidate_requests` separately through success and raise paths, per-call/per-criterion aggregates, sanitized diagnostics, consumed counters, durable JSONL, and an optional report column. It must remain non-billable, must not drive UsageLimits, and must be available on failure even when no `ModelResponse` was produced. Required oracles: retry success, fallback success/exhaustion, native-to-prompted downgrade, and pre-model failure across in-memory result, diagnostic, aggregate, JSONL, and one-row-per-operation summary.

This strengthens the existing recommendations without adding a new maintainer choice: aggregate successful retry usage; narrowly re-raise only the exact Rebar-owned output error in Pydantic's cause chain; add truthful logical candidate count without redefining `requests`.
